open_points.subject: source of an action's today
open_points.text: “takes today's date as that instant's UTC date itself” contradicts “operations reads the action's one instant and today's date from clock”; clock offers only “recorded_now” and “monotonic_reading”
open_points.question: Must operations derive today from the single recorded_now instant, or must clock provide a separate current-date reading despite offering no such capability?
options: derive the UTC date from the action's single recorded_now instant
add or improvise a separate clock reading for today's date
open_points.default_guess: Derive the UTC date from the action's single recorded_now instant.

witness.initial: A Customer is not ended, and the owner submits an end date of 2026-11-17 immediately before midnight UTC on 2026-11-16.
events: The owner submits the mark action with end date 2026-11-17.
operations reads the action instant as 2026-11-16T23:59:59.999999Z.
UTC midnight passes before a separate date reading could occur.
customers checks whether the supplied end date is later than today.
outcomes: Deriving today from the action instant yields 2026-11-16, so the action is refused.
Reading today separately after midnight yields 2026-11-17, so the action is accepted.

set_aside.subject: retention of the configured owner credential
set_aside.text: “module:runtime_settings and module:configuration, which load and check them, are the only other modules that keep them” contradicts “no other module keeps it”
set_aside.question: After startup, does module:runtime_settings retain the owner credential, or must module:configuration be the only module that keeps it while owner_sessions and random_values receive it only for a comparison?
options: runtime_settings retains the credential alongside configuration
runtime_settings discards it after loading and only configuration retains it
set_aside.default_guess: Discard it from runtime_settings after configuration has checked and retained it.

witness.initial: A start has passed configuration checks and the instance is serving the owner interface.
events: The host starts Registry and module:runtime_settings reads the owner credential.
module:configuration checks and retains the credential.
The owner submits a sign-in and module:owner_sessions requests the credential for comparison.
outcomes: runtime_settings still holds another copy of the credential after startup
runtime_settings no longer holds the credential after handing the settings to configuration
witness.observer: a host memory inspection, crash-dump review or security test

set_aside.subject: retention of configured service tokens
set_aside.text: “module:runtime_settings and module:configuration, which load and check them, are the only other modules that keep them” contradicts “module:configuration gives it the checked tokens, and no other module keeps them”
set_aside.question: After startup, does module:runtime_settings retain the service tokens, or does only module:configuration retain them while service_access and random_values receive them transiently for each identification?
options: runtime_settings retains the tokens alongside configuration
runtime_settings discards the tokens after loading and only configuration retains them
set_aside.default_guess: Discard the tokens from runtime_settings after configuration has checked and retained them.

witness.initial: A normal start has passed and the service API is serving requests.
events: The host starts Registry and module:runtime_settings reads all configured service tokens.
module:configuration checks and retains the tokens.
A service calls a project read and module:service_access asks configuration for the tokens for that identification.
outcomes: runtime_settings still holds another copy of every service token
runtime_settings holds no service token after startup
witness.observer: a host memory inspection, crash-dump review or security test
